statements.status_notes: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a symlink traversal vulnerability in the libacl pathname-based functions acl_get_file(), acl_set_file(), acl_extended_file(), and acl_delete_def_file() that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing any pathname component with a symbolic link. Attackers who control any component of a pathname processed by a privileged caller can redirect ACL read or write operations to arbitrary files or directories, enabling unauthorized manipulation of access control lists and local privilege escalation.
statements.impact_statement: libacl symlink-traversal vulnerability in acl_get_file/acl_set_file/acl_extended_file/acl_delete_def_file, which Ubuntu has marked Ignored (backport deemed too intrusive; needs new acl_*_at() APIs). Requires a privileged (root) caller invoking ACL functions on attacker-influenced paths; this container runs unprivileged (docker/Dockerfile:72) and never calls ACL functions.

statements.status_notes: acl before version 2.4.0 contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that allows local attackers to escalate privileges by replacing a pathname component with a symbolic link between an lstat() check and subsequent symlink-following operations such as stat(), chown(), chmod(), acl_get_file(), and acl_set_file(). Attackers who control a pathname component can redirect file access control list operations to arbitrary files when getfacl, setfacl, or chacl is invoked by a privileged process over an attacker- controlled path, resulting in local privilege escalation.
statements.impact_statement: libacl time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition allowing local privilege escalation by replacing a pathname component with a symlink, which Ubuntu has marked Ignored (same reasoning as CVE-2026-54369). Requires a privileged (root) caller invoking ACL functions; this container runs unprivileged (docker/Dockerfile:72) and never calls ACL functions.
